trials.notes: Correctly uses WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), checks null, walks tokens, reads ordinary #text plus whitelisted TITLE/TEXTAREA opening tags, excludes SCRIPT/STYLE, and uses decoded get_modifiable_text() with UTF-8-safe truncation. All called HTML API methods are documented; no _doing_it_wrong records.

Correct processor and documented token-walk pattern. It handles decoded text, special TITLE/TEXTAREA opener text, null processor creation, and UTF-8 truncation. Minor style deduction because the special-element branch relies on get_token_name() rather than first checking get_token_type() === '#tag', but this did not cause misuse or failures.

Uses the right processor and documented methods, and passes all tests. Minor deductions: it calls is_tag_closer() on every non-text token instead of only after confirming a #tag token, and its substr() fallback can split UTF-8 if mb_substr() is unavailable. No hallucinated HTML API usage and no _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: No failed hidden cases: all three execution.json files report 10/10 passing with no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs did well on the key decision points: the processor-choice guidance says to use WP_HTML_Processor for structure and text extraction from BODY fragments; create_fragment() documents the BODY-fragment factory and null return; the text-extraction recipe says ordinary DOM text is #text tokens only unless special-element content is explicitly requested; next_token() explains text can be split across tokens and that SCRIPT/STYLE/TITLE/TEXTAREA carry text on opener tokens; get_modifiable_text() states #text, TITLE, and TEXTAREA are decoded while SCRIPT/STYLE are raw. Near misses were not hidden-test failures: trial-2 and trial-3 could have been more precise by guarding special-element handling with #tag, and trial-3's byte-oriented fallback would violate codepoint truncation outside an mbstring-capable runtime.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs describe the current tag token case but do not explicitly state the behavior or recommended precondition when a next_token() loop is currently matched on text, comments, or doctypes.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Document that callers in token walks should normally guard with get_token_type() === '#tag' before applying tag-opener/closer logic, and state the return behavior on non-tag tokens.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::get_modifiable_text() and the DOM-style text extraction recipe
doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain broad modifiable text and opt-in special elements, but the decision surface is spread across prose and examples.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact general table mapping #text, TITLE/TEXTAREA openers, SCRIPT/STYLE openers, comments, and processing instructions to decoded/raw status and whether they are ordinary DOM text or opt-in/non-DOM text.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs recommend mb_* with explicit UTF-8, but do not explicitly warn that byte-oriented strlen()/substr() are invalid for codepoint limits.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a sentence that returned text is UTF-8 and must be measured/sliced with UTF-8-aware APIs for codepoint limits; byte functions can split characters.

doc_gaps.problem: Null creation, get_last_error(), and paused_at_incomplete_token() are documented, but there is no concise checklist for read-only extraction policy after a scan.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short policy checklist: handle null creation, walk tokens, then deliberately choose best-effort accumulated output, empty/null, or error behavior when get_last_error() or paused_at_incomplete_token() is set.
